children: Shares of GrafTech International surged after the company said it was hiking prices for its graphite electrodes by at least 30%, effective immediately.
The stock rose 17% to $7.24 in Tuesday morning trading. The stock has fallen 53% since the start of the year.

The price increase, which impacts all open commercial negotiations, comes after three years of falling graphite electrode prices and rising input costs, the company said. Cost-cutting efforts, including capacity idling and workforce reductions, "alone are not sufficient to restore sustainable economics," the company said.

"Our graphite electrode pricing remains at levels that we do not believe are sustainable or consistent with the investment required to provide customers with reliable, high-quality supply over the long term," Chief Executive Timothy Flanagan.
The price hike builds on a previous price increase GrafTech implemented in March.
The company said late last month that it would close a graphite electrode manufacturing facility in Monterrey, Mexico and sell the underlying property, citing structural overcapacity in the industry.
